items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: I was playing with some great people like Henry “Red” Allen, Coleman Hawkins, Gene Krupa, all those older cats.

ctx.x: I wanted to talk about that, yeah.

Okay. So what happened was the first night I played the Metropole Marty Napoleon was Louis Armstrong’s pianist at the time. And he was the house pianist there. And he went out in the neighborhood and next thing I knew man, about five piano players in the neighborhood were sitting there right at the bar listening to me play. And I said, “Man, this ain’t Florida, this is for me, New York.” And so when the Salt City Six left the Metropole hired me as one of the house pianists. I just stayed here. And that’s how it…
